candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, monitoring, adverse effects and client medication teaching.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication deprescribing and patient teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients that transient rebound symptoms can occur when long-term PPIs are stopped and that either tapering or abrupt discontinuation may be considered when deprescribing is appropriate.

options.A: Use an exact eight-week taper for every long-term PPI user because any faster reduction causes permanent pathologic acid hypersecretion.
options.B: Explain that transient rebound upper-GI symptoms may occur after long-term PPI discontinuation and that either dose tapering or abrupt discontinuation can be considered.
options.C: Never stop a PPI abruptly because rebound symptoms are uniformly dangerous and cannot be managed clinically.
options.D: Continue the PPI indefinitely after the original indication has resolved because long-term duration alone creates a maintenance indication.

candidate.rationale: AGA Best Practice Advice states that patients who discontinue long-term PPI therapy should be advised that transient upper-GI symptoms may occur from rebound acid hypersecretion and that either dose tapering or abrupt discontinuation can be considered. Patients without a definitive chronic indication should be considered for a trial of deprescribing. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: When long-term PPI therapy no longer has a clear indication, deprescribing may be considered; clients should be warned about transient rebound symptoms, and tapering or abrupt discontinuation are both acceptable approaches.
candidate.source_document_title: De-prescribing proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) — Clinical Practice Update
candidate.source_locator: Best Practice Advice 2, 8, and 9: patients without a definitive chronic indication should be considered for deprescribing; warn of transient upper-GI symptoms due to rebound acid hypersecretion; either dose tapering or abrupt discontinuation can be considered.
candidate.source_version_date: Published February 16, 2022; live guidance rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A client has taken a proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) long term but no longer has a clear ongoing indication. Which deprescribing teaching is most accurate?
